records.title: HEALTH MELAS .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)
(a) to (c) Health Melas have been organised in Mathura (17-20 September, 2000), Delhi (16-25 October, 2000), Kargil (21-25 October, 2000) and Patna (19-21 November, 2000) with a view to provisioning integrated quality health care services, to meet the unmet needs among all segments of population. In these melas people become aware of a number of options before them in terms of the different systems of medicine (allopathy, homeopathy, ayurveda and unani). People begin to comprehend the linkages between preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative health care and also the linkages between the primary, secondary and tertiary health sectors. People are getting sensitised to the role of Central Government, the State Government, the elected local bodies, the NGOs and the professional organisations. The pre-mela demographic and epidemiologial surveys provide vast amounts of data about a given city and its rural hinterland.
 The State Government did not consider it advisable to hold the mela in October/November, 2000 as the State was goving through election to local bodies. The `Health and Family Welfare Mela` is proposed to be organised at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh from 31st January to 2nd February, 2001.
 The Health and Family Welfare Melas are proposed to be held in the States, which have weak socio-demographics indices.

details:
(a) whether it is a fact that IAS Officers working in States
and Union Territories have opened private Non-Government
Organisations in the name of social service and thus amassing
massive Government grants and others donations due to their
influence and access;
(b) whether Government have so far taken or are considering
to take any action against the officers involved in such an
erroneous affairs after identifying them and ascertaining their
source of income; and
(c) if so, the details of the action taken against them and
if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND
DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS` WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF
PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE) 
(a) : As provided in the AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968, the IAS
officers working in States require previous sanction of the
concerned Governments before associating themselves in any manner
with Non-governmental Organisations, if such organizations are
aided by the Central Government, State Government or an
international organization or agency. This information is
therefore not maintained centrally. In respect of officers
working in the Union Territories, such permission is required to
be granted by the Ministry of Home Affairs. So far, no IAS
officer working in the Union Territories has been granted such
permission.
(b) &(c) : Regarding IAS officers working in the States, the
concerned State Governments are competent to initiate action
against such officers for any violation of these provisions of
the AIS(Conduct) Rules, 1968.

records.title: INCOME TAX COLLECTION FROM WINNERS AND ORGANISERS OF KAUN BANEGA CROREPATI. OIH
details:
(a) whether Government are collecting Income Tax on the 
amount won by winners in the most popular programme
`Kaun Banega Crorepati`.
(b) if so, the percentage amount of income tax;
(c) whether Government have collected Income Tax from 
the sponsors and producers of the said programme; if so,
the amount collected separately from sponsors and
producers; and
(d) if not, the reasons and purpose for not collecting
Income Tax from sponsors and producers of the programme.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)
 (a) & (b):- The amount won by winners in 
the programme `Kaun Banega Crorepati` is taxable @ 40%
plus sur-charge under Section 115BB of the Income-tax
Act, 1961. However, there is no provision for deduction
of tax at source on such winnings.
 (c) & (d):- The producers of the said programme
are regular corporate assessees and are assessed to tax over 
the years. Since the programme has started only in the current
financial year, income and tax thereon from this will be
known only after the Return of Income for the relevant
period i.e. Assessment Year 2001-02 is filed which
will be due on 30th November, 2001.
 Further, the sponsors are well known companies
and are all asessed to tax. However, these sponsors who 
are advertising on TV programme are only incurring expenditure. 
Since there is no income involved, there is no tax liability 
in the case of sponsors.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI E.PONNUSWAMY)

records.title: UNDUE FAVOUR BY PRASAR BHARATI TO AN AUSTRALIAN COMPANY .
details:
(a) whether Prasar Bharati has been giving undue favour to an Australian Company `Nain Broadcasting` directly 
and indirectly since past some time and an objection also has been raised in this regard by Parliamentary Standing 
and Advisory Committee: 
(b) if so, whether Government in view of the objection raised by both Parliamentary Committees, would take 
speedy action after conducting a proper enquiry about the activities of Prasar Bharati and Nain Company from the 
beginning till date and cancel the agreement with the said company; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therfor?

THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
(SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)
(a) to (c) : No Sir. Prasar Bharati has intimated that M/s Nine M/s Network Australia Pty Ltd. has been awarded 
contract for telecasting certain programmes on DD-2 channel for the 7.00 PM to 9.00 PM slot after they made the 
highest bid for the said slot offering a bid amount of Rs. 59.00 crores against the floor price fixed at Rs. 55.00 
crores. The same company through M/s Nine Broadcasting India Private Ltd. has also been granted the 9.00 PM to 
10.00 PM slot for DD-2 after they successfully quoted the a bid of Rs. 62.00 crores against the Floor price of Rs. 
42.5 crores fixed for the said slot. The programmes are also being repeated on the following day, morning 
transmission of DD-2, from 9.00 AM to 12.00 Noon.
Prasar Bharati has also intimated that M/s Nine Network of Australia has also been awarded a contract for 
production of live signals of international cricket events to be held in India, for international production companies, 
after the bid for the said production was found best, economical and suitable by Prasar Bharati after proper 
evaluation.
During presently ongoing examination by the Standing Committee on Information & Technology about 
functioning of Prasar Bharati, issue of agreement with M/s Nine Network, Australia, has also come up but as yet 
Standing Committee on Information Technology has not given any report objecting to this decision of Prasar 
Bharati.
The Policy of the Government is that Prasar Bharati is competent to take its own decisions in autonomous 
manner in programme matters in view of scheme of governance envisaged in Prasar Bharati Act.

records.title: INDIAN TEACHERS IN NEPALI SCHOOLS .
details:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)
(a) to (d) A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (A) TO (D) OF THE ANSWER TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 78 TO BE ANSWER ON 23.11.2000 ON `INDIAN TEACHER IN NEPALI SCHOOLS`.
In view of non-availability of full information or records in this regard, precise estimates of the number of Indian citizens working as teachers in the schools of Nepal is not possible. The government, however, work on the basis of a figure approximately of 1000 plus, as a guide.
The Government of India is not aware of any attempts to remove Indian teachers from their jobs. However, a majority of the Indian teachers have not been granted permanent status so far, they continue to work on an ad hoc and temporary contractual basis, which deprives them of facilities such as provident fund, increments, pension, voluntary retirement benefits, promotion, medical reimbursement, etc., benefits that are available to their Nepalese counterparts. 
The issue of regularisation of service of the Indian teachers in Nepal has been discussed on a number of occasions between the Government of India and His Majesty`s Government of Nepal, including at the highest level. During the visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India in June 1990, it was agreed that the Indian nationals employed in schools in Nepal would be placed on the same footing as Nepalese nationals as regards the terms and conditions of employment. This assurance has been reiterated by the Nepalese side during subsequent high-level exchanges as well. 
In 1990-91, the Nepalese Cabinet had decided that as a one-time exception, all teachers who were working for at least five years in various Government schools till the previous year, would be made permanent. In accordance with this decision, it is estimated that about 100 Indian teachers were made permanent. In 1998, His Majesty`s Government of Nepal issued a notification whereby the Indian teachers working in Nepalese schools, who have completed one year of service by 1990-1991 and have still been working on temporary basis, would not be removed on the basis of nationality alone. The notification also stated that those teachers who would like to retire or who voluntarily quit their position or who were removed for reasons other than nationality, shall be granted a lumpsum benefit depending on their length of service. 
The issue was again raised with the Prime Minister of Nepal, Mr. G.P. Koirala, during his visit to India in August 2000. A Joint Press Statement issued on August 3, 2000 during the visit stated that His Majesty`s Government would implement the decisions taken in 1998 in this regard. Meanwhile, the Government of India continues to take up specific problems of the Indian teachers with His Majesty`s Government of Nepal through diplomatic channels.

The Government has taken adequate care of the kith

(b) Public Distribution System (PDS) is implemented under the joint responsibility of the

records.title: (clubbed) REHABILITATION OF CHILD LABOUR .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether Government have received a report entitled `Child
Labour, Education and Rehabilitation` submitted by the Centre of
Concern for Child Labour as reported in the Hindustan Times on the 4th
April, 2000;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that only 4 lakh children in
hazardous employment are rehabilitated as against promise to
rehabilitate two million children in 2000;
(c) whether as per Ministry of Labour record there were 44 million
child workers in 1991, if so, what is the number thereof at present in
the country; and
(d) what are Government`s concrete plans for their rehabilitation
during the year 2000-2001?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT ( SHRI MUNI LALL )
(a) to (d) : Centre of Concern for Child Labour has submitted a
report to the Government in April, 2000. The report inter-alia,
contains details on definition of Child Labour, extent of child labour,
types of child labour, Government of India`s Policy towards child
labour, rehabilitation of child labour through different models and
challenges for future.
 Authentic information on Child Labour is generated during the
decennial Census. As per the 1991 census, the total number of working
children in the country is 11.28 million.
 Government of India has been implementing two schemes, for
rehabilitation of Children withdrawn from work, namely the scheme of
National Child Labour Projects (NCLP) and the scheme of Grant-in-aid to
Voluntary Organisations. 92 NCLPs are currently under implementation
in 10 child labour endemic states for rehabilitation of 1.9 lakh
children. Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs ( CCEA )in its meeting
held on 20.1.99 approved the continuance of the scheme of NCLP for the
duration of the Ninth Plan and expansion of number of projects to 100.
 Under the Scheme of Grant-in-aid, funds are released to
Voluntary Organisations, on the recommendation of the concerned State
Government, for taking up action oriented projects for the benefit of
working children. Over 70 projects are currently under implementation
under the Scheme of grant-in-aid.
 The above Schemes are continuing in the year 2000-2001 also.
 Government is committed to the goal of eradication of child
labour in all its forms. Considering the nature and magnitude of the
problem a gradual, progressive and sequential approach has been adopted
to withdraw and rehabilitate child labour.

records.title: RISE IN CRIME DUE TO INFILTRATION .
details:
(a) the reaction of Government on the news-item captioned `Sakht Qanoono Ke Karan Pak Nahin Jaate Bangladeshi` appearing in the `Dainik Jagaran` dated 10th March, 2000; and
(b) the steps Government are contemplating to take in order to check incidents of prostitutiion and other crimes which are on the rise due to foreign infiltrators ?

MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS ( SHRI L.K. ADVANI )
(a): In view of the long and porous border with Bangladesh and also on account of various push and pull factors, many Bangladeshis have managed to sneak into various parts of the country. Due to ethnic and linguistic similarities, they are able to mingle easily with the local population.
 As per available reports, some Bangladeshi immigrants cross over to Pakistan in search of better livelihood. About 3846 Bangladeshi infiltrators have been apprehended along the Indo-Pak border since 1997 (till March 2000).
 Various measures have been taken to check infiltration. These include, inter alia, construction of border roads, border fencing, raising of additional battalions of the Border Security Force, intensification of patrolling along the border, increase in the number of outpost towers, provision of surveillance equipment including night vision devices, etc. The matter has also been taken up with the Government of Bangladesh at various levels from time to time. There are standing instructions to the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to detect and deport foreigners staying illegally.
(b): Instructions have been issued to the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to deal firmly with those found violating the law of the land.

details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER
( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )
(a) to (e) : National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) received 
two bids under International Competitive Bidding (ICB) for Main 
Plant Package for Stage-II of Kavas and Gandhar power projects in 
Gujarat. Both the bidders did not meet qualifying requirements 
relating to Joint Deed of Undertaking and took major deviations 
on various specifications, operational functional guarantees, 
completion schedule and other important conditions of the bid 
rendering the bids non-responsive.
Keeping in view national importance of these 
projects and for ensuring their timely completion during the 
Ninth Plan period, NTPC was advised by the Ministry in the public 
interest to finalise the bids by negotiating with the bidders on 
the basis of a legal opinion taken from the Additional Solicitor 
General. However, NTPC, taking into account certain major 
deviations on various specifications and requirements, treated 
both the bids as non-responsive and decided to rebid. Government 
has left the matter to the NTPC Board being a Navratna Company 
for a decision. A review of bidding conditions has been 
undertaken by NTPC and rebidding is being done by providing 
adequate time to the bidders for better competition and response.

details:

STATEMENT AS REFERRED TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 296 FOR ANSWER ON 15.3.2000.
(a)to(c): No Statewise record regarding the number of security and police personnel killed in landmine blasts, is maintained by the Central Government . However, the Government of India and the concerned State Governments continuously review the situation arising out of militancy, terrorism, insurgency and extremist activities. 
 In order to tackle cross-border terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir, Government of India has implemented an action plan. For neutralising militancy / terrorism in the North-East various steps including deployment of CPMFs and Army, improved coordination and intelligence sharing between security forces, modernisation/upgradation of State Police Forces etc. have been undertaken.
For effectively countering Left Wing Extremism, the affected States of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa were requested to prepare integrated action plans encompassing the development as well as security aspects of the problem for the affected areas. The States have also been advised to take vigorous follow-up action. The Government of India has also set up a coordination centre headed by the Union Home Secretary with Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of the States affected by Left Wing Extremism, as its members, to review steps taken to check the Left Wing Extremist activities, monitor the plan of action in respect of each state etc.
In addition, in order to minimise attacks due to landmine and / or IED blasts on security forces/police personnel/civilians, steps such as deployment of road opening parties, use of metal detectors, mine protected vehicles etc. are being taken.

(a) & (b): The non plan revenue expenditure in 2000-2001 is 
estimated to be Rs. 228768 crore compared to Rs. 204904 crore

growth and bring about structural changes in the composition of
expenditure the Union Budget for 2000-2001 have announced several
initiatives. These among other include rigorous zero base budgeting 
scrutiny of all ongoing schemes, reassessment of manpower requirements

review of all subsidies, earmarking portion of disinvestment proceeds
for retiring government debt etc. Besides, for medium term management
of the fiscal deficit a committee has been set up to examine and make 
suitable recommendations for a strong institutional mechanism embodied 
in a Fiscal Responsibility Act. For expenditure management and 
restructuring an Expenditure Commission has also been set up.

MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)
PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT

.PA
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a), (b), (c) AND (d) OF RAJYA
SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2399 SLATED FOR 23.12.1999
REGARDING APPOINTMENT OF SUCCESSFUL OBC CANDIDATES 
(a), (b), (c) & (d) : Union Public Service Commission 
(hereinafter referred to as UPSC) had recommended a total of 215
candidates belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) for
appointment on the basis of the Civil Services Examination (CSE)
1997 : of these, 166 candidates had been recommended by relaxed
standards for the 166 vacancies reserved for OBCs, whereas 49
candidates belonging to OBC category were recommended as part of
the list of general category candidates as they had qualified the
CSE 1997 without availing any of the concessions/relaxations
available for the OBCs.
The combined order of merit declared by UPSC forms the
basis of service allocation to 28 different services/posts having
regard to the position in order of merit, order of preference for
the available services, category-wise vacancy, status on medical
fitness and previous employment. In the course of allocation of
service, it was found that out of the 49 OBC candidates, who had
been recommended as part of the list of the general category
candidates, only two could be allocated to a service of their
higher preference without availing the benefit of reservation for
purposes of service allocation and were, as such, adjusted
against unreserved vacancies. The remaining 47 candidates,
however, who could be allocated to the service of their higher
preference only through relaxed standards for purposes of service
allocation were given the benefit of reservation for the purpose
of allocation to a service of their higher preference and, hence,
were adjusted against OBC vacancies in that service. As such,
there were 213 (166+47) OBC candidates available for allocation
to the 166 reserved vacancies for the OBCs. Of these 213 OBC
candidates -
(a) 166 OBC candidates were allocated to various services;
(b) 30 OBC candidates were ineligible for allocation as they
either had already accepted allocation to a service on the basis
of an earlier Civil Services Examination and had not qualified
for allocation to services/posts which were higher in the order
of preference as per Rule 18 of the CSE, 1997 Rules, or were
declared physically unfit by Medical Board for appointment;
(c) the remaining 17 OBC candidates could not be allocated to a
service on the basis of CSE 1997 due to the non-availability of
vacancy at their turn in the merit order under the OBC category.
3. The manner of service allocation followed by the 
Government is strictly in accordance with the ratio laid down by 
the Hon`ble Supreme Court in the case of Ritesh R.Shah (JT 1996 
(2) SC 495); M. Neethi Chandra (1996 6 SCC 36) and Dr. Anil 
Kumar (1998 9 SCC 405). Some of the recommended OBC candidates
who could not be allocated to a service also agitated the matter 
before CAT Hyderabad Bench (A. Murali Manohan and N. Vijay 
Bhaskar) and CAT Principal bench (Satya Prakash and Anil Kumar)
and both the benches of the CAT upheld the manner of service 
allocation as followed by the Government.

records.title: DISCUSSION WITH PAKISTAN ON THE NUCLEAR RESTRAINT
details:
(a) whether Government of Pakistan have proposed a discussion with India on the 
nuclear restraint,
(b) if so, the extensive details of the said proposal and whether Government 
have taken any step towards fixing the time and venue for a discussion on the 
proposal; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, what stand has been taken by 
Government on the said proposal of Pakistan?

THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH) 
(a-c) As part of the composite dialogue process, India and Pakistan are holding 
discussions on Peace and Security, including Confidence Building Measures. 
During the first round of discussions on this subject, in October 1998, various 
proposals were exchanged, including proposals by Pakistan on nuclear restraint 
India drew Pakistan`s attention to our security needs which flow naturally from 
our size, location and assets and are not one country-specific. We also 
emphasised that our defence posture was non-aggressive. In this context, India 
proposed the upgradation of existing CBMs and the need to put into place new 
CBMs in the nuclear and conventional fields. Government have also declared that 
India shall maintain a credible minimum nuclear deterrent, pursue a no first use 
doctrine, observe a moratorium on farther nuclear test explosions and refrain 
from engaging in an arms race. India`s approach, therefore, is one of exemplary 
restraint and moderation.
During the visit of Prime Minister to Pakistan on 20-21 February 1999, Prime 
Minister and the Prime Minister of Pakistan signed the Lahore Declaration in 
which it was agreed that the two countries would take immediate steps for 
reducing the risk of accidental or unauthorised use of
nuclear weapons and discuss concepts and doctrines with a view to elaborating 
measures for confidence building in the nuclear and conventional fields, aimed 
at the prevention of conflict. On this occasion, a Memorandum of Understanding 
was also signed between the Foreign Secretaries of India and Pakistan under 
which both countries have Agreed to lake measures and conclude agreement 
wherever necessary to build confidence in the nuclear and conventional fields. 
It has also been agreed in the Memorandum of Understanding that the technical 
details will be worked out by experts of the two sides in meetings to be held on 
mutually agreed dates before mid`99.

records.title: TALKS WITH USA .
details:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH) 
(a) We have been engaged in an ongoing dialogue with the United States since June, 1998. The dialogue is being conducted through Shri Jaswant Singh, Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission and Mr.Strobe Talbott, US Deputy Secretary of State. Six rounds of talks have been held so far. Fourth round of talks was held in the third week of August. 
(b) The talks were held from August 20-21, in Washington. There was also a brief follow-up meeting in New York on-August 29, 1998. 
(c) The talks are being conducted on the basis of the comprehensive proposals that India has put forward on disarmament and non-proliferation matters comprising our unilateral moratorium on explosive nuclear tests, our willingness to discuss converting this moratorium into a de jure obligation, our offer to enter into constructive negotiations on the FMCT and our determination to make more stringent the existing system of export controls over sensitive material and technology.
The dialogue has resulted in some progress. India has firmly conveyed its security concerns as well as the need for India to-maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent. These talks are predicated on this basis. There now exists some understanding for India`s concerns and requirements.
After six rounds, the talks have narrowed, and are now focussed on four issues, which are mainly centered around the proposals which India had initially put forward. These issues are the CTBT, the FMCT, Export Controls and Defence Posture. 
(d) Two more rounds of talks were held after August 1998, -in September (21) and November(19-20), in Washington and Rome respectively. In addition, an expert-level meeting was also held on the subject of Export Controls in New Delhi on 9-10 November, 1998 as a part of the ongoing dialogue. Both sides have agreed to meet in the second half of January, 1999 in New Delhi to carry forward this process.

records.title: EFFECTS OF REPLACEMENT OF FERA WITH FEMA
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to replacement
of Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) by the Foreign
Exchange Management Act, !998 (FEMA) the morale of those
involved in the embezzlement of foreign exchange has
become high and it will result in more cases of
embezzlement of foreign exchange;
(b) whether it is also a fact that `sensitive`
and `very sensitive` cases will be examined under FEMA; and
(c) if not, the way in which Government propose
to check the embezzlement of foreign exchange by taking
action against the persons involved therein and to
examine the sensitive and very sensitive cases.

MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA) 
(a) : No, Sir. 
(b) & (c) : The cases of embezzlement are dealt
with under the normal criminal laws and that even under
the existing FERA, 1973 and the proposed FEM Bill, 1998
there does not exist any provision to tackle and take
care of the aspect of embezzlement of foreign exchange.
Further, the violations/contraventions committed
after coming into force of FEMA would be governed by the
provisions of FEMA. Even though FERA is repealed when
FEMA comes into force: Clause 49(3)(a) of FEM Bill
provides that offences/contraventions of repealed Act
committed during the currency of that Act would be
governed by the provisions of the repealed Act as if that
Act has not been repealed. Thus as per the existing
provisions of the Bill, cases of contraventions whether
`sensitive` or `very sensitive` committed during the
currency of FERA would be governed by the provisions of
FERA and those committed when FEMA comes into force will
be governed by the provisions of FEMA.

MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI MOHD. MAQBOOL DAR)
(a) to (c) As per provisions of the SPG Act, as amended, SPG is responsible for providing `proximate security` to the Prime Ministers and the members of his immediate family as also the former Prime Minster and members of their immediate families for a period of 10 years from the date of demission of their office. The immediate family members include wife, husband, children and parents. Therefore, the lady VIPs enjoying SPG protection will continue to get such protection even after marriage.
